findings.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the new abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data, leaving it uninstantiable. StatefulDetectorHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data is decorated @abc.abstractmethod in src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py; the MetricAlertDetectorHandler body is just `pass`, so any call to group_type.detector_handler(detector) (via Detector.detector_handler in models/detector.py) raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class with abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data — the metric alert detector path crashes instead of returning a handler.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler declares `pass` while inheriting StatefulDetectorHandler, which now declares `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (and `get_dedupe_value`/`get_group_key_values` via the abstract base contract) as @abc.abstractmethod, so any code path that instantiates it (e.g. the grouptype registry's detector_handler instantiation on Detector.detector_handler) raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class with abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data. Any detector whose type resolves to the metric-alert grouptype crashes at handler construction instead of evaluating, replacing the previous working (if stubbed) list-returning behavior; nothing in the diff implements or tests the new abstract hook for this handler.

[ADVISORY] build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a `value` parameter but never uses it, and the tests exploit this: test_state_results_multi_group builds the expected group_2 occurrence with value 6 when the packet supplied 10, and test_results_on_change uses 6 against an actual value of 100 — so the value actually passed by evaluate_group_key_value into the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook is completely unverified. A regression that passes the wrong group value (e.g. the dedupe value, another group's value, or 0) into build_occurrence_and_event_data would pass the entire suite; the next developer extending the hook to embed value in evidence_data gets no test signal about correct value propagation.

[ADVISORY] The resolve path (new_status == OK producing a StatusChangeMessage fed to create_issue_occurrence_to_kafka) has no process_detectors-level verification: the new tests mock produce_occurrence_to_kafka and assert calls only for PayloadType.OCCURRENCE, and the StatusChangeMessage result path (evaluate with value 0 crossing below threshold) is asserted only at the handler.evaluate level, never through the process_detectors/produce path this diff restructured. A regression in create_issue_occurrence_from_result's handling of the StatusChangeMessage variant (e.g. passing the wrong payload_type or dropping the status_change payload) ships undetected; users whose detectors resolve never get the resolution event.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is a `pass` subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of the three abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so it cannot be instantiated. Any code path that constructs MetricAlertDetectorHandler (i.e. any detector with type slug "metric_alert") raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class — the PR's stated goal of metric alerts producing occurrences is unreachable, and the pre-existing empty-but-working evaluate() implementation was deleted in the process.

[ADVISORY] The multi-group test builds occurrence_2 with value 6 while group_2's actual evaluated value is 10, and the assertion still passes, proving the `value` argument flowing into build_occurrence_and_event_data is never verified. A regression that passes the wrong value (or drops it) into build_occurrence_and_event_data would go undetected; the same pattern recurs in test_results_on_change (line ~491) where value 100 is compared against an occurrence built with value 6.

[ADVISORY] PriorityLevel(new_status) performs a raw cross-enum cast from DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel with no invariant that the two enums' member values actually align, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data contract (PriorityLevel-typed status) is only exercised via this cast. If a DetectorPriorityLevel value is added or renumbered without a matching PriorityLevel member, every occurrence produced by the new hook fails with ValueError at evaluation time, and no test in the diff pins the mapping.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler extends StatefulDetectorHandler while implementing none of its abstract methods, so instantiating it raises TypeError. Any metric-alert detector whose `type` slug resolves to this grouptype will fail at `detector_handler` construction/`process_detectors` with 'Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods build_occurrence_and_event_data, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values' — previously it returned a no-op empty list; every evaluation of a metric alert detector now crashes instead of being a no-op.

[BUG] PriorityLevel(new_status) coerces a DetectorPriorityLevel enum to PriorityLevel by value, silently assuming the two enums share value semantics. If any DetectorPriorityLevel member value has no PriorityLevel counterpart (or maps to a different severity), build_occurrence_and_event_data receives a wrong/unrepresentable priority that is written into the occurrence's initial_issue_priority — a wrong-priority issue is created with no error. The conversion is untyped and unchecked at the API boundary between the two priority enums.

[ADVISORY] The new abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data was added to the DetectorHandler-adjacent StatefulDetectorHandler interface, breaking every out-of-tree or not-yet-updated implementer of the base contract. DetectorHandler subclasses in other parts of the codebase not shown in this diff that don't implement the new abstract method will fail at import/instantiation time; the diff only updates the test mock and the (still-broken) MetricAlertDetectorHandler, so any other StatefulDetectorHandler implementer is left on the old signature and its evaluation path dies with TypeError.

[ADVISORY] The local variable `result` is annotated as a union of the message types but reuses the same name for both StatusChangeMessage and IssueOccurrence branches, and the `result is not None` check in process_detectors now gates on a value that is always non-None on the occurrence path. Future readers/consumers conflating `result.result` (payload) with the evaluation result container get a subtle trap: the previous `result = None` sentinel meaning 'no payload' was removed, so any caller that previously distinguished 'no result' from 'status change' by None-ness now treats every non-OK transition as an occurrence-producing result, changing which paths reach create_issue_occurrence_from_result.

[BUG] The diff silently deletes the duplicate-group-key detection and error logging that the previous design treated as an invariant to investigate, replacing it with silent last-write-wins semantics in a dict keyed by group_key. In evaluate() (results[result.group_key] = result), a handler that returns two results for the same group_key now overwrites the first with no log, so a duplicate-emitting detector silently drops a state update/occurrence where the prior code logged "Duplicate detector state group keys found" for operators to investigate; the paired test test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was also deleted, so no test covers this path at all.

[ADVISORY] The refactor changes the DetectorHandler.evaluate abstract contract from list[DetectorEvaluationResult] to dict[DetectorGroupKey, ...] and removes result=None as the "no occurrence" signal, but the local annotation `result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence` is still non-exhaustive-looking and the result-is-None branch in process_detectors is retained as dead-or-ambiguous typing for downstream implementers. Any out-of-tree or not-yet-migrated DetectorHandler subclass (the abstract method is public API within the codebase) breaks silently: its list-returning evaluate still satisfies no type check at runtime, so process_detectors calls detector_results.values() on a list and crashes with AttributeError while iterating results in `for result in detector_results.values():` — the MetricAlertDetectorHandler was updated in this diff but the contract change is invisible to any other implementer.

[BUG] The test mock's build_occurrence_and_event_data discards its `value` parameter, so no test in the diff verifies that the correct group value is propagated to the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook. MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data (lines ~34-37) forwards `value` to build_mock_occurrence_and_event, but that helper (bottom of file) never uses `value` in constructing the occurrence — initial_issue_priority comes from new_status, fingerprint from group_key. This is proven by the tests themselves: test_results_on_change evaluates group value 100 (and test_dedupe value 8, test_state_results_multi_group group_2 value 10) while the expected occurrence is built with value=6, and the assertions still pass. A regression in evaluate_group_key_value that passes the wrong value (or a hardcoded constant) to build_occurrence_and_event_data would go completely undetected by this suite, and downstream consumers building evidence/value-bearing occurrences from the hook would ship with silently wrong values.

[ADVISORY] TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change and TestEvaluate.test_dedupe construct expected occurrences with value=6 while the code under test was fed value=100 and value=8 respectively, encoding the wrong expected value into the test data even though the discarded-parameter mock makes it pass. Future readers/maintainers copying these expected-value patterns into a real handler whose occurrence actually uses `value` (e.g. a subtitle or evidence field) will inherit tests that assert occurrence content built from the wrong input value, failing confusingly or masking propagation bugs. The next change to make the mock value-aware gets harder and riskier because every expected value in this file is currently wrong relative to the input.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is declared as a subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing any of the abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating it raises TypeError; its previous concrete evaluate stub is deleted. Any detector whose type slug resolves to the metric-alert group type will crash the handler constructor in detector.detector_handler / process_detectors with 'Can't instantiate abstract class ... with abstract methods', so every data packet for that detector fails instead of being evaluated (previously it evaluated to no results via the []). The new abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data added in this diff makes the missing implementation load-bearing.

[ADVISORY] PriorityLevel(new_status) performs an enum value conversion from DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel with no mapping guard, so any DetectorPriorityLevel whose numeric value is not a valid PriorityLevel value raises ValueError inside evaluate_group_key_value. If the two enums ever drift in value assignment (e.g. a new DetectorPriorityLevel member added without a matching PriorityLevel), every non-OK evaluation for detectors of that priority crashes the whole process_detectors loop, aborting state commits and occurrence production for all subsequent detectors in the batch; there is no try/except or test covering a non-HIGH priority.

This is a concrete test gap introduced/retained by the diff, not an immediate production bug.

This is a value-based enum cast that can raise `ValueError` if `DetectorPriorityLevel` and `PriorityLevel` values ever diverge. The tests added exercise only the `HIGH` path (via `condition_result=DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH` and expected `PriorityLevel.HIGH`), but they don’t explicitly pin or validate the full mapping/invariant between the enums beyond that single member, so the review concern about the fragility of this contract is diff-grounded even if an actual mismatch isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new @abc.abstractmethod `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` to `StatefulDetectorHandler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py). Any concrete subclass must now implement it (and the other abstract methods). However, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` and is now just `pass` (src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py), meaning it does not implement the required abstract methods (including the newly added one). If anything tries to instantiate this handler (via `Detector.detector_handler`), it will raise a `TypeError` about abstract methods, i.e., broken behavior introduced by the diff. Claims about other out-of-diff implementers are plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes the stateful detector path to *always* attach a payload on a non-OK transition by introducing `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` and setting `result` to either a `StatusChangeMessage` (OK branch) or an `IssueOccurrence` (else branch) before returning `DetectorEvaluationResult` (see `evaluate_group_key_value`). `process_detectors` iterating `for result in detector_results.values(): if result.result is not None: create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` is consistent with that change, and the updated tests explicitly assert `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` is called for HIGH transitions. The finding’s claim about callers previously distinguishing by `None`-ness and now being subtly broken is not verifiable from this diff; no such caller behavior is shown here. The variable-name reuse is at most a readability nit, not a demonstrated defect.

In evaluate() (results[result.group_key] = result), a handler that returns two results for the same group_key now overwrites the first with no log, so a duplicate-emitting detector silently drops a state update/occurrence where the prior code logged "Duplicate detector state group keys found" for operators to investigate; the paired test test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was also deleted, so no test covers this path at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit duplicate-group-key detection/logging in `process_detectors` (the loop over a list and `logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found", ...)`) and changes the contract so `evaluate()` returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate()` populates it via `results[result.group_key] = result`, which is inherently last-write-wins. However, with the new API duplicates are no longer representable at the `process_detectors` boundary (a dict can’t contain duplicate keys), and in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate()` the inputs come from `group_values.items()` where `group_values` is itself a dict, so the previously tested “duplicate keys from input” scenario can’t occur in the same way. Still, the change does remove an invariant check/observability for accidental overwrites, and the corresponding dupe test was deleted, so this is a concrete regression in diagnostics rather than a clearly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor changes the DetectorHandler.evaluate abstract contract from list[DetectorEvaluationResult] to dict[DetectorGroupKey, ...] and removes result=None as the "no occurrence" signal, but the local annotation `result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence` is still non-exhaustive-looking and the result-is-None branch in process_detectors is retained as dead-or-ambiguous typing for downstream implementers. Any out-of-tree or not-yet-migrated DetectorHandler subclass (the abstract method is public API within the codebase) breaks silently: its list-returning evaluate still satisfies no type check at runtime, so process_detectors calls detector_results.values() on a list and crashes with AttributeError while iterating results in `for result in detector_results.values():` — the MetricAlertDetectorHandler was updated in this diff but the contract change is invisible to any other implementer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the `DetectorHandler.evaluate` abstract signature to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (and updates `process_detectors` to iterate `detector_results.values()`), so any existing subclass still returning a `list` would raise `AttributeError` at runtime. However, the diff does not show whether any other non-updated `DetectorHandler` implementations exist in the codebase, so the claimed crash is a migration/compatibility risk rather than a directly verifiable defect from this PR alone. The note about the retained `if result.result is not None` check being potentially redundant is also grounded but not itself a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test mock's build_occurrence_and_event_data discards its `value` parameter, so no test in the diff verifies that the correct group value is propagated to the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook. MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data (lines ~34-37) forwards `value` to build_mock_occurrence_and_event, but that helper (bottom of file) never uses `value` in constructing the occurrence — initial_issue_priority comes from new_status, fingerprint from group_key. This is proven by the tests themselves: test_results_on_change evaluates group value 100 (and test_dedupe value 8, test_state_results_multi_group group_2 value 10) while the expected occurrence is built with value=6, and the assertions still pass. A regression in evaluate_group_key_value that passes the wrong value (or a hardcoded constant) to build_occurrence_and_event_data would go completely undetected by this suite, and downstream consumers building evidence/value-bearing occurrences from the hook would ship with silently wrong values.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract hook `StatefulDetectorHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, new_status)` and calls it from `evaluate_group_key_value` with the computed `value`. However, in tests the mock implementation ultimately calls `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)`, whose `value` parameter is unused when constructing the `IssueOccurrence`/`event_data`. This is visible in multiple tests: e.g. `test_results_on_change` evaluates `group_vals` of 100 but builds the expected occurrence with `value=6`, and assertions still pass. So the suite does not verify that the correct group value is propagated into the new hook—this is a real, diff-grounded test gap, not a demonstrated functional defect in the production code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change and TestEvaluate.test_dedupe construct expected occurrences with value=6 while the code under test was fed value=100 and value=8 respectively, encoding the wrong expected value into the test data even though the discarded-parameter mock makes it pass. Future readers/maintainers copying these expected-value patterns into a real handler whose occurrence actually uses `value` (e.g. a subtitle or evidence field) will inherit tests that assert occurrence content built from the wrong input value, failing confusingly or masking propagation bugs. The next change to make the mock value-aware gets harder and riskier because every expected value in this file is currently wrong relative to the input.

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/.../test_detector.py`, `TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change` calls `handler.evaluate(...{"val1": 100}...)` but builds the expected occurrence via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)`. Similarly, `test_dedupe` feeds `{"val1": 8}` but builds the expected occurrence with `value=6`. Since `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` currently ignores its `value` parameter, the tests still pass, but the expected-value patterns are inconsistent with the inputs and could mislead future, value-aware occurrence assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is declared as a subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing any of the abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating it raises TypeError; its previous concrete evaluate stub is deleted. Any detector whose type slug resolves to the metric-alert group type will crash the handler constructor in detector.detector_handler / process_detectors with 'Can't instantiate abstract class ... with abstract methods', so every data packet for that detector fails instead of being evaluated (previously it evaluated to no results via the []). The new abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data added in this diff makes the missing implementation load-bearing.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` with an `evaluate()` stub to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` is (and remains) abstract and now additionally requires `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` (added as a new `@abc.abstractmethod`), alongside other abstract methods (`get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, etc.). Because `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` implements none of these, it is not instantiable and would raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` when `Detector.detector_handler` tries to instantiate `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (see `Detector.detector_handler` using `self.group_type`). Thus any detector whose `type` slug maps to the metric-alert group type will crash during processing rather than returning empty results as before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PriorityLevel(new_status) performs an enum value conversion from DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel with no mapping guard, so any DetectorPriorityLevel whose numeric value is not a valid PriorityLevel value raises ValueError inside evaluate_group_key_value. If the two enums ever drift in value assignment (e.g. a new DetectorPriorityLevel member added without a matching PriorityLevel), every non-OK evaluation for detectors of that priority crashes the whole process_detectors loop, aborting state commits and occurrence production for all subsequent detectors in the batch; there is no try/except or test covering a non-HIGH priority.

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the diff adds `PriorityLevel(new_status)` when building an occurrence (`result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel(new_status))`). Since `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel`, this relies on the two enums having compatible underlying values; otherwise `PriorityLevel(...)` can raise `ValueError`, and there is no local guarding/handling in `evaluate_group_key_value` or `process_detectors`. However, the diff does not show the enum definitions, so an actual mismatch/crash is not verifiable from this PR alone—it's a robustness/maintenance concern exposed by the change rather than a confirmed defect.
